title: Demurrage and Detention Free Time: Overdue Portfolio Balance and Free-Time Purchases
content:
## Rule

A request to buy more free time on a Demurrage and Detention Free Time record is weighed against the customer's demurrage and detention position across all of its records, not against the one container alone. Whether an upgrade can be sold turns on one comparison: the customer's overdue demurrage and detention balance against the overdue threshold of the product the customer wants to buy. At or below that threshold the sale may go ahead; above it, it may not. The threshold belongs to that product, never to the product already on the record.

## What the overdue balance is

The overdue balance is taken from the state of all of the customer's free-time records on the day the request is handled. It is the total balance still due on those records that stand invoiced and whose invoice is past due.

- An invoice counts as **past due** from the day after its payment term, reckoned from the invoice date, runs out; the date compared is the handling date.
- The **payment term** is set by the product the record carries, as a number of calendar days running from the invoice date. Where the customer is credit-approved and the customer's credit days exceed that term, the credit days are used instead.
- A **submitted** dispute against an invoice keeps that invoice out of the past-due set.
- Money owed in other product categories, booking charges and documentation fees among them, stays outside this total in **every** case.

Every one of these facts is read from the company's records for the customer, and the test is made before the purchase is booked.

## Judgement table

| Overdue balance compared with the threshold of the product being bought | Upgrade purchase |
|---|---|
| lower | permitted |
| exactly equal | permitted |
| higher, by any amount | not permitted |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical figures)

- A threshold of 1000.00 and an overdue balance of 1000.00: permitted, since the balance does not exceed the threshold. At 1000.01 the purchase is not permitted.
- An invoice dated 1 March with an assumed term of 12 days is not past due when handled on 13 March and is past due when handled on 14 March.
- A customer who is credit-approved with 20 credit days, on a product whose term is taken as 12 days: the invoice is judged against 20 days. With 10 credit days the product's 12 days are used, because the credit days are not longer.
- An invoice already past its term but carrying a submitted dispute adds nothing to the overdue balance.
